title: Dhanaraj verdict: Former CPM MLA criticises judiciary, invokes Cheemeni killings in warning to acquitted RSS workers
content: Kannur: The Taliparamba Sessions Court on Wednesday (November 25) sentenced three RSS workers to life imprisonment for hacking to death CPM activist C V Dhanaraj, while acquitting 16 others for want of evidence. The court also criticised the police investigation and the influence of a CPM branch secretary on it. Responding to the verdict, former Payyannur MLA T I Madhusoodanan criticised the judiciary, questioned the court's assessment of a prosecution witness and invoked the Cheemeni killings while warning those acquitted. Speaking at a DYFI-organised Kuthuparamba martyrs' commemoration in Payyannur on Wednesday night, the CPM Kannur district secretariat member said the party would settle scores. His remarks referred to the 16 acquitted accused, all RSS workers, and those criticising the party on social media. If we have to settle scores, we will settle scores. This movement has no hesitation in that, he said. He then referred to the 1987 Cheemeni killings in Kasaragod, in which five CPM workers were killed after a mob set fire to the party office during the Assembly election. The courts, the government machinery and those who ridicule us must remember that in the Cheemeni incident, not a single person was convicted by any court. But they must also understand that those people are no longer alive, he said. On March 23, 1987, Congress worker Plantholi Krishnan was stabbed to death at Kayyur during a clash with CPM workers. News of his killing triggered a violent reprisal at nearby Cheemeni, where a mob of Congress workers set the CPM local committee office on fire after trapping party workers inside. Five CPM workers who tried to escape were hacked and stabbed to death. The case against 53 Congress workers ended in acquittal, with criminal lawyer C K Sreedharan, then with the Congress, appearing for the defence. Three men suspected by the CPM of involvement in the attack, M M Jose, K P Surendran and Abraham, were subsequently murdered, allegedly by CPM workers. Sreedharan later joined the CPM in 2022 and was appointed special public prosecutor by the LDF government in the Dhanaraj murder case. The Cheemeni acquittal also featured in his autobiography, which was released by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan. Criticism of the judge The former MLA also took exception to the use of verses attributed to Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish at the beginning of the judgment. The verses reflected on the human cost of violence and the families left waiting for loved ones. He accused the judiciary of acting in the interests of the establishment. "We can see that the judiciary, as part of the government establishment, is also implementing a policy of crushing progressive and Left politics in the interests of the establishment," he alleged. Despite the criticism of the judiciary, Madhusoodanan thanked the court for rejecting the defence suggestion that he was involved in Dhanaraj's murder. The court relied on the testimony of Dhanaraj's mother and wife and the bloodstained clothes of the first three accused to convict them. Court's assessment of the witness Madhusoodanan questioned the court's assessment of the prosecution's first witness, P P Prajeesh, a CPM branch secretary and neighbour of Dhanaraj. He was an eyewitness to the incident. He was the first witness. But the court was not convinced by what he said, Madhusoodanan said. He alleged that the court had refused to accept Prajeesh's testimony because he was a CPM worker. The judgment, however, examined inconsistencies in Prajeesh's account over 17 paragraphs rather than relying on his political affiliation alone. Prajeesh claimed he had seen 11 people in and around Dhanaraj's house. Dhanaraj's mother and wife, who were present during the attack, identified only three assailants. His account also referred to people arriving on motorcycles, which the victim's mother and wife did not corroborate...
